 Ba1 No. 834 of 2025

Hon'ble Alok Mahra, J.
Mr. Rohit Kakkar and Mr. Ravindra S. Rawat, learned counsel for the applicant.
2. Mr. Deepak Bisht, learned D.A.G. for the State.

3. The applicant - Abhishek Kumar, who is in judicial custody in connection with FIR/Case Crime No. 235 of 2024, under Sections 323, 376(2)(n), 420, 504 and 506 of IPC, registered at P.S.-
Mukhani, District Nainital, has sought his release on bail.

4. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the records.
5.
In this case, an FIR was lodged by the complainant wherein she has alleged that she is a Government Servant working in Bhimtal while applicant is working in some private bank.
As per the contents of the FIR, the applicant used to go with the complainant on her scooty from Haldwani to Bhimtal on daily basis and he also used to ask for money quite often from the complainant.
On 23.02.2020, the applicant took the complainant to his room in Haldwani and drugged her and sexually assaulted her and thereafter made videos of her in compromising position.
Thereafter, he threatened the complainant that if she would not heed to his demand, then, he would make the videos viral.

In the FIR, the allegations have been levelled against the father of the applicant in which it is alleged that even the father has sexually assaulted and raped the complainant by threatening her of making the videos viral.
Allegations against the family members are also made in the FIR.

6. Learned counsel for the applicant would submit that all the allegations are false and fabricated;
that applicant never had any physical relations with the complainant nor does he have any obscene videos of the complainant.
It is further submitted that applicant is in custody since 11.02.2025.
7. Learned State Counsel, on the other hand, has vehemently opposed the bail application.

Though,
as per the instructions received, learned State Counsel would fairly admit that no such video was recovered from the mobile phone nor any bank transaction was found between the complainant and the applicant.

8. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the records.

1 9.
Prima facie, this Court finds that a report submitted by the State does not corroborate with the allegations levelled in the FIR.

10. Having considered the submissions, under the facts and circumstances of the case and also considering the fact that no such video was recovered from the mobile phone nor any bank transaction was found between the complainant and the applicant, this Court is of the view that it is a case fit for bail and the applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail.
11. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.
12. Let the applicant be released on bail on his executing a personal bond and furnishing two reliable sureties each of the like amount, to the satisfaction of the court concerned.

(Alok Mahra J.) 25.03.2026 Ujjwal BA1/834/2025 on 25 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104879541/
